question_text: A street vendor bought 50 mangoes for P750 and sold each at P20. What is the percentage profit?

hint_ladder.title: Cost Per Mango
hint_ladder.text: Total cost P750 for 50 mangoes. Cost per mango = P750 ÷ 50 = P15.

hint_ladder.title: Profit Per Mango
hint_ladder.text: Selling price per mango is P20. Profit per mango = P20 - P15 = P5.

hint_ladder.title: Profit Percentage Formula
hint_ladder.text: Percentage profit is based on cost: (Profit per mango / Cost per mango) × 100%.

A.text: You might have chosen A because you used selling price as base: P5/P20=25%, but profit % uses cost.

B.text: You might have chosen B because you rounded 33.33% down or miscalculated cost, ending up with 30%.

C.text: Correct. Cost per mango is P15, profit per mango P5; (5/15)×100 = 33.33%.

D.text: You might have chosen D because you used an incorrect cost base or added error from total revenue, giving 40%.

next_time_rule: **Key Takeaway:** Profit % = (Profit per unit / Cost per unit) × 100%. Always divide by cost, not selling price.
deconstruct_text:
Alam mo ba, parang nagtitinda ka ng mangga sa palengke ng Balintawak? Bumili ka ng 50 piraso sa halagang ₱750. Ang puhunan bawat isa: 750 ÷ 50 = ₱15. Kapag ibinenta mo ng ₱20 isa, tubo = ₱5 bawat mangga.

Para sa profit percentage, ang base ay COST, hindi selling price. Tubo / Puhunan × 100% = (5/15) × 100% = 33.33%. Tama ba? Oo, 1/3 ng puhunan ang kinita mo.

**Watch-Out Zone: wrong_base_percentage** in action. P5/P20=25% ay markup, not profit %.
